method: Mapped each advertised tier to independent proof obligations for a local span finding, a positive relationship finding (cycle), a set-completeness finding (blast radius), a negative finding (dead code), and full replay. For each, asked what retained object lets a later consumer verify why the predicate held without consulting mutable caches or the live repository.
answerToAuthorsDoubt: No. T1 as cited source spans does not answer why for relationship, completeness, or absence claims. The tiered-and-declared direction is sound; the T1 definition and default are not.

resolves.B-RT-01: OPEN-BLOCKER: cited spans prove neither a relationship path nor completeness/absence; T1 is proof-incomplete for shipped rule classes.
resolves.B-RT-02: OPEN-BLOCKER: T0's retained 'facts' are undefined. If it retains fact bodies it may already contain the proof and is not tiny; if it retains only identities/digests it cannot support the advertised queries.
resolves.B-RT-03: OPEN-BLOCKER: T1 cannot be the universal default until a rule-family proof matrix and negative controls demonstrate proof completeness and bounded privacy cost.
resolves.B-RT-04: OPEN-BLOCKER: an immutable sealed Run cannot contain a mutable currentTier that degrades after GC.
resolves.B-RT-05: OPEN-BLOCKER: relationship and negative proof capsules may be large and source-bearing, so the unconditional 'small fraction' and 'small' claims are unproved.
resolves.B-RT-06: OPEN-BLOCKER: T2 read-set bytes do not by themselves permit full re-derivation; historical providers, toolchains, environment inputs, schemas, and deterministic execution must remain obtainable.
resolves.B-RT-07: OPEN-BLOCKER: T1 default excerpt retention contradicts threat-model V4/R7's explicit, default-off excerpt materialisation.

counterexamples.whyRequires: an ordered closed witness path, relation kinds, node identities, and provenance for every edge
counterexamples.whySpansFail: one or more cited lines do not establish that the edges resolve to the claimed nodes or close the cycle

counterexamples.whyRequires: the start set, traversal relation/direction, exact graph view, Coverage, and either the relevant closure or a verifiable commitment/certificate
counterexamples.whySpansFail: a sampled path can prove membership but cannot prove the returned set is complete

counterexamples.whyRequires: entrypoint/public-surface policy, semantic universe, searched reference relation, exact Coverage, dynamic-resolution limits, and a closed-world absence certificate
counterexamples.whySpansFail: the declaration span proves the symbol exists; it cannot prove no qualifying reference exists

findings.requiredChange: Replace T1-excerpt with T1-proof. A finding retains a typed, predicate-specific proof capsule: positive witness subgraph and edge provenance where applicable; exact predicate/query identity; Coverage and universe commitments for negative or complete-set claims; source excerpts only when the proof actually needs source text.
findings.whatWouldChangeMyMind: A worked T1 object for all three counterexamples that a later verifier can check using only retained T1 state.

findings.evidence: T0 says it retains facts, findings, Coverage, and identities, while also claiming it cannot answer why and remains tiny.
findings.impact: The word 'facts' can mean full immutable fact chunks, selected fact identities, or only digests. Those choices have opposite privacy, size, and explanatory consequences.
findings.requiredChange: Give each retained field a schema-level custody form: body, identity, digest/commitment, or reference with retention state. Define whether Coverage bodies and set commitments remain available after cache GC.
findings.whatWouldChangeMyMind: A field-level T0 manifest showing exactly which object bodies survive and demonstrating both the tiny-size and no-why claims.

findings.evidence: The default is selected from a lint-shaped example and no conformance matrix covers relationship, absence, external-scanner, aggregate, or multi-finding proofs.
findings.impact: Retention only tightens. A user discovers that the default discarded necessary proof when recovery is impossible.
findings.requiredChange: Keep the default undecided until every shipped predicate family supplies a T1 proof schema, a positive verification case, a mutation the verifier rejects, a measured size/privacy distribution, and an explicit answer for unsupported proofs. Permit per-finding proof capability with a Run-level minimum/summary rather than pretending every finding has the same evidence shape.
findings.whatWouldChangeMyMind: A representative proof corpus showing T1-proof verifies every shipped class while meeting a published privacy/size budget.

evidence: architecture/02 defines Run as an immutable sealed manifest
RT-1 puts the retention tier in that sealed manifest
RT-2 says the Run records a current tier that mutates T2->T1->T0 as data expires
findings.impact: Either the sealed Run mutates, or its current availability claim becomes stale.
findings.requiredChange: Put immutable requested/sealedTier and proof inventory commitments in the Run/EvidenceDigest. Represent current availability in a separate append-only retention ledger or signed retention event, resolved at read time and never hashed back into the historical Run.
findings.whatWouldChangeMyMind: A precise split already intended by 'records' but absent from the current text.

findings.evidence: A cycle can cite many edges; a blast-radius proof can approach the graph partition; an absence certificate may require a universe/set commitment; each anchor can expose paths, symbols, and source.
findings.impact: T1 can approach T2 size for graph-heavy findings and can retain more sensitive metadata than the 'small fraction' rationale admits.
findings.requiredChange: Remove categorical size labels. Budget proof capsules, deduplicate shared witness objects, privacy-class every member, disclose truncation as proof unavailability rather than silently weakening proof, and measure representative workloads.
findings.confidence: high on possibility, medium on prevalence until measured
findings.whatWouldChangeMyMind: Representative measurements bounding proof closure far below read-set retention for the target workload.

evidence: architecture/02 conditions equality on toolchain and environment identity
P-4a leaves the Rust substrate and packaging unresolved
an identity proves which producer ran but does not make that executable available later
findings.impact: A T2 Run may be called attestation-grade/full-replay even when the historical provider or toolchain cannot be obtained or executed.
findings.requiredChange: Rename the guarantee to input-complete unless the Run also pins retrievable producer/provider binaries, schemas, toolchain/sysroot/lock inputs, environment contract, and a supported replay executor. Make replay capability independently testable from byte retention.
findings.whatWouldChangeMyMind: A delivery/versioning contract guaranteeing offline retrieval and execution of every historical derivation dependency within the declared support window.

findings.evidence: Threat model V4/R7 says excerpt materialisation is explicit and off by default; this section automatically retains excerpts at the default tier.
findings.impact: The same default is simultaneously a privacy violation and a product requirement.
findings.requiredChange: Resolve jointly with B-TM2-01. A proof tier must distinguish non-source structural witnesses from source-bearing excerpts and record the user's forward-only retention choice.
findings.whatWouldChangeMyMind: A normative distinction showing that the retained T1 object is not materialised source content.

recommendedTierShape.T0-manifest: Immutable claims, identities, digests/commitments, exact retention-state references, Coverage summary plus commitments; answers what and which identities, not why.
recommendedTierShape.T1-proof: T0 plus typed predicate-specific proof capsules sufficient for later verification: source excerpt only for local textual claims; witness graph/provenance for positive relations; universe/Coverage/set commitments for negative or complete-set claims.
recommendedTierShape.T2-input-complete: T1 plus all read-set bytes. Call it replay-capable only when the historical executable/toolchain/environment contract is also available and verified.

sealedPropertiesCovered.assessment: Tiered, declared, forward-only retention is accepted as a direction; the tier semantics/default are rejected.
RT-2 violates it unless current availability is moved outside the sealed Run.
Negative and completeness proofs require retained exact-Coverage commitments, not only projected summaries.
Privacy minimisation and real inventory remain binding; automatic excerpt retention currently conflicts with V4/R7.

checksThatCouldHaveFailed: A cycle could have been verifiable from a single canonical anchor if the anchor resolved to a retained witness object; no such object is defined.
T0 could have specified digest-only facts and avoided the size ambiguity; it does not.
T2 could have pinned replay executables/toolchains through delivery/versioning; it does not.
knownLimitations: No representative proof-size corpus exists, so the review rejects the categorical size claim rather than supplying replacement thresholds.
A cryptographic absence proof could make some negative claims compact, but no such proof system or canonical universe commitment is designed here.
I inspected agents-log.md only after this derivation was complete; see the independence disclosure in threat-model.v2.review-b.json.
whatWouldChangeOverallVerdict: A revised section with field-level tier schemas, immutable-vs-current retention separation, proof-complete T1 examples and mutation tests for local/relational/negative/set-complete claims, measured privacy/size bounds, and an honest T2 replay dependency contract.
